questions.q: What does Chapter 2 (Delta Lake) add on top of plain Parquet, in one sentence?
options: A transaction log providing real ACID transactions, schema enforcement, time travel, and safe MERGE
A completely new file format unrelated to Parquet
Row-level and column-level security
A declarative dependency graph
questions.explain: Chapter 2's whole thesis: Delta wraps Parquet with a transaction log, and everything else follows from that.

questions.q: How does Chapter 3's medallion architecture relate to Data Engineering Foundations?
options: It's Foundations' raw/cleansed/curated zones, renamed bronze/silver/gold and made concrete with real Delta tables
It's a completely unrelated concept never mentioned in Foundations
It replaces Foundations' zone concept entirely with something different
It only applies to streaming data, not batch pipelines
questions.explain: This is exactly what Lesson 25 established at the start of Chapter 3.

questions.q: What does Chapter 4 (Unity Catalog) add to everything built in Chapters 1-3?
options: Governance — the real three-level namespace, access control, automatic lineage, and volumes — layered on top without changing existing code
A requirement to rewrite every table created in earlier chapters
A replacement for Delta Lake's transaction log
New PySpark transformation methods not covered in Foundations
questions.explain: Chapter 4's whole premise: governance layered on, not a rewrite of anything already working.

questions.q: How does Chapter 5 (Lakeflow) relate to the pipeline built in Chapter 3?
options: It's the same pipeline, declared instead of imperatively wired, with data-quality rules built in as decorators
It's a completely different pipeline with no relationship to Chapter 3's work
It replaces Delta tables with a different storage format
It only applies to Unity Catalog governance, not actual transformations
questions.explain: Lesson 48 named this directly: Autoloader, foreachBatch/MERGE logic, and jobs/tasks all map onto Lakeflow's pieces.

questions.q: What is still true about every PySpark method (select, filter, groupBy) from Data Engineering Foundations, after this entire course?
options: It still works, completely unchanged, inside a @dlt.table function today
It has been entirely replaced by new Lakeflow-specific syntax
It only works within Chapter 1's compute lessons, not later chapters
It requires Unity Catalog governance to function at all
questions.explain: Nothing from Foundations was replaced — this course named the platform and added guarantees, architecture, and governance on top.
